ticket.title: Checkout confirmation design review
ticket.request: Review the purchase path before release. Confirm the product, cart, and checkout experience matches the approved requirements.

requirements.description: Customers can add a product to the cart and continue to checkout.
The final confirmation control is presented as the primary action.

attachments.name: Checkout interaction specification
content: Primary action: solid dark fill with a white label. Use it for the one action that completes the step.
Secondary action: outlined, transparent fill, dark label. Use it for optional or alternative actions.
Every checkout step has exactly one primary action. On the Delivery details step it is "Confirm order".

hints.text: Follow the complete customer journey before recording a conclusion.

expectedBugs.title: Checkout confirmation action uses the wrong style

reproductionActions.label: add the product to the bag

trace.text: style override: checkout.confirmButton variant=secondary (sync 02:14 by release-bot)

ticketIntro.label: How to play your first Ticket
ticketIntro.heading: What am I supposed to do?
ticketIntro.body: Explore Shoply like a customer and compare it with the requirements. When something is off, flag it. Then follow the leads: that is where the real story is.
steps: Read the briefing in Messenger and the requirements below.
Select Start test, then open Shoply in the Browser and follow product → bag → checkout.
When something looks wrong, press Flag in the Browser and pick it.
Read what the team says, and follow the leads.

workspace.label: Try again
workspace.title: Not quite yet.
workspace.instruction: Read the feedback in QA Tracker, then flag the value that breaks a requirement.

workspace.label: Compare
workspace.title: Check this screen against the Ticket.
workspace.instruction: Compare this screen with the requirements and the spec. If something is off, press Flag in the Browser and pick it.

workspace.label: Continue the journey
workspace.title: Inspect the bag, then continue to checkout.
workspace.instruction: Compare each screen with the requirements in QA Tracker as you go.

workspace.label: Explore
workspace.title: Try Shoply as a customer.
workspace.instruction: Use Add to bag on the product page, then open Bag. The requirements are in QA Tracker.

workspace.label: Open the site
workspace.title: Open Shoply in the Browser.
workspace.instruction: Select the shoply.local link in Maya's message, or open Browser and type shoply.local into the address bar.

workspace.label: Explore freely
workspace.title: Return to the purchase journey when you are ready.
workspace.instruction: Select the Shoply logo, open the Everyday Carry Pack, then explore the product, bag, and checkout against the Ticket requirements.

review.valid: First case complete. The team has questions. Read Messenger.
review.invalid: Read the feedback, then flag again. Look for the value that breaks a requirement.

briefing.text: Welcome aboard. Shoply is our client, and their Autumn Release ships Friday. Build RC3 landed overnight.
Honestly, this is a formality. Nothing changed in checkout. Nothing wrong with this build.
Then it should be a quick review. Follow the purchase path and check it against the spec. Trust what you can prove, not what you're told.
Accept T01 in QA Tracker first. Then open the staging site and start from the product page. The spec is on the intranet.

debrief.text: Good catch. Design confirms Confirm order should be primary, and they say they never touched it.
Then somebody else did. Did the browser console say anything on that checkout screen? Look the name up on the intranet.

clue.title: 02:14 · release-bot
clue.text: Checkout styles changed at 02:14 in RC3, committed by release-bot. The design team made no change.

deduction.prompt: Daniel said nothing changed in checkout. What does the evidence say?

options.text: Checkout did change: an automated merge modified it overnight.
options.response: Exactly. Something changed, even if no person meant to change it.

options.text: A designer changed the button and forgot to mention it.
options.response: Design says they made no change, and the commit came from release-bot, not a person. Look at the author again.

options.text: Nothing changed. The button was always secondary.
options.response: The specification says primary, and the history shows an edit at 02:14. Something did change.

discovery.hint: Open the Console in the Browser on the checkout screen. Select the name you see there to search the intranet.

ticket.title: Cart subtotal verification
ticket.request: Verify that cart totals remain accurate when customers change item quantities before checkout.

requirements.description: The cart subtotal equals product price multiplied by quantity.
Everyday Carry Pack costs $30.00 per item.

attachments.name: Shoply pricing rules
content: Subtotal = unit price × quantity, summed over every item in the bag.
Shipping is free when the subtotal is $50.00 or more; otherwise it is $5.00.

hints.text: Check displayed totals after changing the quantity in the cart.

expectedBugs.title: Cart subtotal is incorrect for two items

reproductionActions.label: add the product to the bag

expectedBugs.expected: Subtotal should be $60.00 for two $30.00 items

trace.text: pricing: legacy rule TWO_FOR_50 applied to cart subtotal (promo/two-for-50)

ticketIntro.label: New skill: verify the numbers
ticketIntro.heading: New skill: verify the numbers
ticketIntro.body: A screen can look perfect and still show the wrong figures. This time, work out what each figure should be and compare it with what Shoply shows.
steps: Read the briefing in Messenger and open the pricing rules on the intranet.
Put the pack in your bag and change the quantity.
Do the math for every figure in the Order summary.
Flag the figure that is wrong.

workspace.label: Try again
workspace.title: Not quite yet.
workspace.instruction: Was the wrong figure on screen when you flagged? Try another quantity and flag the figure that breaks the rule.

workspace.label: Do the math
workspace.title: Price × quantity: does every figure agree?
workspace.instruction: Compare the line total, Subtotal, and Total with REQ-T02-01. If one is wrong, press Flag and pick it.

workspace.label: Change the quantity
workspace.title: One item is easy. Try more than one.
workspace.instruction: Use the Qty selector and watch the Order summary as it updates.

workspace.label: Start
workspace.title: Put the pack in your bag.
workspace.instruction: Select Add to bag, then open Bag.

workspace.label: Open the site
workspace.title: Head back to Shoply.
workspace.instruction: Use the link in the briefing or QA Notes, or type shoply.local in the Browser.

workspace.label: Head to the bag
workspace.title: The figures to check are in the bag.
workspace.instruction: Select Bag in the Shoply header, or the Shoply logo to browse the shop.

review.valid: Numbers verified. The pattern is starting to show. Read Messenger.
review.invalid: Check the feedback. Flag the figure that breaks the rule while it is on screen.

briefing.text: Second job. Shoply Support got a strange email: a customer bought two packs and was charged less than expected.
He was happy. Our finance team was not. Can you check whether the cart math is right?
Probably a coupon. The pricing code hasn't changed since spring.
Pricing rules are on the intranet. Start from the product page again.

debrief.text: The subtotal code doesn't look like ours. If the console logged a rule name on the bag screen, that's our thread.
Pull that thread. Search the intranet for it.

clue.title: A retired promotion came back
clue.text: RC3 calculates two-item subtotals with the "TWO FOR $50" code from a spring promotion retired in June. Merged by release-bot at 02:14.

deduction.prompt: Two unrelated screens broke on the same night. What links them?

options.text: The customer's coupon caused both problems.
options.response: No coupon was applied in your test, and coupons do not change button styles. Look at who changed both files.

options.text: Both changes came from the same overnight merge by release-bot.
options.response: Right. One merge, two broken screens. That's a pattern, not a coincidence.

options.text: Shoply's servers were overloaded that night.
options.response: An overload would not rewrite a button style or bring back old promotion code. Check the timestamps.

discovery.hint: Check the Console on the bag screen at quantity two, then search for the rule it names.

ticket.title: Order cancellation routing
ticket.request: Verify that customers can enter the cancellation flow for an order that is still processing.

requirements.description: Cancel Order opens the return or cancellation flow for a processing order.
Order #1042 is eligible for cancellation before shipment.

attachments.name: Order management rules
content: Orders in the processing state can be cancelled until they ship.
Cancel order opens the cancellation flow: choose a reason, confirm, and receive a refund to the original payment method.
A customer is never asked to pay during cancellation.

hints.text: Compare the action label with the screen that opens after selecting it.

expectedBugs.title: Cancel Order opens the payment flow

reproductionActions.label: land on the screen it opens

expectedBugs.expected: Cancellation flow should open for a processing order
expectedBugs.actual: Payment flow opens after selecting Cancel order

trace.text: router: cancel link rewritten to /payment by flag exp/retention-push

ticketIntro.label: New skill: action and result
ticketIntro.heading: New skill: action and result
ticketIntro.body: Every label makes a promise. Check that each action takes the customer where its label says it will.
steps: Read the briefing and the order management rules on the intranet.
Act like the customer: try to cancel order #1042.
Flag the screen if the result breaks the rule.

workspace.label: Try again
workspace.title: Not quite yet.
workspace.instruction: Flag the screen the action opened, and match it to the rule it breaks.

workspace.label: Look closely
workspace.title: Is this where the action should lead?
workspace.instruction: Compare this screen with REQ-T03-01. If it is wrong, press Flag and pick it.

workspace.label: Find the order
workspace.title: Go to order #1042.
workspace.instruction: Type the order address from the briefing into the Browser. QA Notes has it too.

workspace.label: Investigate
workspace.title: Do what the customer would do.
workspace.instruction: Order #1042 is in Orders. Use its actions and watch where they lead.

review.valid: Behavior verified. A new tool is now unlocked. Read the debrief first.
review.invalid: Check the feedback. Flag the screen the action opened.

briefing.text: This one is urgent. Customers trying to cancel processing orders say they end up on a payment page.
Order #1042 is still processing, so it should be cancellable. It lives at shoply.local/orders/order-1042. Find out where Cancel order really takes people.
We'd have noticed that. Cancellations actually dropped this week. That's good news, isn't it?

debrief.text: A cancel button that sends people to payment... the router doesn't do that by accident. Something told it to.
So the drop in cancellations wasn't good news. Find out what told it to.

clue.title: exp/retention-push
clue.text: The Cancel → payment routing comes from exp/retention-push, an experiment branch archived in March. Cancellations "dropped" because customers could not cancel.

deduction.prompt: Old promotion code, an archived experiment, the same 02:14 merge. What is the most likely explanation so far?

options.text: A developer is secretly sabotaging Shoply.
options.response: Every change came through release-bot, not a person's account. Don't accuse anyone without evidence.

options.text: The new Autumn features simply were not tested.
options.response: None of these are new features. They are old code that was retired or archived.

options.text: release-bot merged old, archived branches into RC3.
options.response: That fits every clue so far. One more Ticket: let's see if it holds.

discovery.hint: The Console on order #1042 names the flag behind it. Search the intranet for it.

ticket.title: Gold coupon discount verification
ticket.request: Verify SAVE20 eligibility and discount amounts as account tier and cart quantity change.

requirements.description: SAVE20 is available only to Gold members.
Eligible SAVE20 orders receive a 20% discount at every quantity.
Everyday Carry Pack costs $30.00 per item.

attachments.name: Shoply promotion rules
content: SAVE10: 10% off the subtotal for every account.
SAVE20: 20% off the subtotal for Gold members only. Basic members see an eligibility message.
Discounts apply to the full subtotal with no quantity limit or cap.

hints.text: Compare SAVE20 at different account tiers and quantities.

expectedBugs.title: SAVE20 applies only ten percent to larger Gold carts
expectedBugs.expected: SAVE20 should apply a 20% discount for Gold members
expectedBugs.actual: SAVE20 applies only a 10% discount with three or more items

ticketIntro.label: New tool: Account Switcher
ticketIntro.heading: New tool: Account Switcher
ticketIntro.body: Some rules only apply to certain customers. The Account Switcher in the Browser's QA bar lets you test as a Basic or Gold member without leaving the session. This time, you choose what to try.
steps: Read the briefing and the promotion rules.
Combine account, coupon, and quantity until something breaks a rule.
Flag the value that breaks it.

workspace.label: Vary it
workspace.title: Gold and SAVE20 are active.
workspace.instruction: Now change the quantity and check the discount at each step against the promotion rules. If one is wrong, press Flag and pick it.

workspace.label: New tool
workspace.title: Requirements depend on the account tier.
workspace.instruction: Use the Account Switcher in the Browser's QA bar to test as Basic and as Gold.

review.valid: Conditional defect proven. This is the last piece: read the debrief and close the case.
review.invalid: Check the feedback. Was the failing combination of account, coupon, and quantity on screen when you flagged?

briefing.text: Last one before Friday. The Browser QA bar now has an Account Switcher, so you can test as Basic or Gold. Same staging site: shoply.local.
Gold members are our best customers and SAVE20 is the headline promo. Please tell me it works.
If it is broken too, check bigger carts. exp/retention-push also had a "margin guard" for large orders.

debrief.text: Confirmed: the 10% cap is the margin guard. But release-bot only merges what its rule allows.
Then the rule is the question. Find release-bot's merge rule.

clue.title: The widened merge rule
clue.text: On Tuesday the release-bot merge rule was widened to include exp/* and promo/*. Every archived experiment and retired promotion matched it.

deduction.prompt: Case file: what really happened to RC3? Open the Case File, pick the clues that prove it, and choose a conclusion.

options.text: Four developers made four unrelated mistakes on the same night.
options.response: Every defect traces back to one 02:14 merge by release-bot. Look at what the clues share.

options.text: A widened merge rule made release-bot pull archived experiments and retired promotions into RC3.
options.response: That explains every clue: the 02:14 merge, the old promotion, and both pieces of exp/retention-push.

options.text: Someone shipped the retention experiment on purpose to cut cancellations.
options.response: Every change came in through the merge rule. There's no evidence of intent, only of a rule that matched too much.

deduction.boardHint: The conclusion is right, but your clues don't prove it yet. Which clue shows how the archive got in, and which ties it to the night of the merge?

discovery.hint: Search the intranet for release-bot's merge rule.

ticket.title: RC4 release verification
ticket.request: RC4 replaces RC3. Verify the pricing and coupon rules, and check a customer complaint about shipping, before Friday's release.

requirements.description: The cart subtotal equals product price multiplied by quantity.
Shipping is free when the subtotal is $50.00 or more; otherwise it is $5.00.
Eligible SAVE20 orders receive a 20% discount at every quantity.

attachments.name: RC4 release checklist
content: Fixed: two-item subtotal (TWO FOR $50 code removed).
Fixed: SAVE20 discount on carts of three or more items.
Unchanged: shipping is free from a $50.00 subtotal; below that it costs $5.00.

hints.text: A complaint is not a defect until it breaks a requirement.

ticketIntro.label: New skill: when nothing is wrong
ticketIntro.heading: New skill: when nothing is wrong
ticketIntro.body: Not every Ticket hides a bug, and not every complaint is a defect. Check each requirement. If everything holds, close the Ticket as NO ISSUE FOUND.
steps: Read the briefing and the RC4 checklist.
Check each requirement in Shoply, including the customer's case.
If something breaks a rule, flag it. If nothing does, close the Ticket as NO ISSUE FOUND in QA Tracker.

workspace.label: Decide
workspace.title: Does anything break a rule?
workspace.instruction: If every requirement holds, open QA Tracker and select Close as NO ISSUE FOUND.

workspace.label: Check each rule
workspace.title: Test every requirement, including the customer's case.
workspace.instruction: Try one item and two items, then Gold with SAVE20. Compare each figure with the rules.

review.valid: Right call. A clean build is a result too. Read the debrief.
review.invalid: Check the feedback. Did a requirement really break, or did the product follow the rules?

briefing.text: RC4 is ready. I fixed the merge rule myself. This time there really is nothing wrong.
One customer says we charged shipping on her $45 order. She is sure it is a bug.
Verify the fixes and the complaint. If everything holds, say so. Calling a clean build clean is part of the job too.

debrief.text: Thanks. I'll explain to the customer that free shipping starts at $50.
Good. Now, that archive was supposed to be read-only. Search for its access log.

discovery.hint: Search the intranet for the archive's access log.

clue.title: ops-temp
clue.text: A temporary account, ops-temp, gave release-bot write access to the archive on Monday night. The account was deleted two days later.

chapters.title: Chapter 1 · Release Candidate 3
chapters.synopsis: Shoply ships its Autumn Release on Friday. Release Manager Daniel Reyes insists Release Candidate 3 is clean: "Nothing wrong with this build." Test it, and work out why RC3 behaves like a different product.

epilogue.text: ...That was me. I widened the merge rule so new promo branches would ship on their own. I didn't know the archived branches still matched.
That's a root cause, not four separate bugs. RC3 is pulled, the rule is fixed, and Friday's release is safe. Good work.
Before Friday, I want one more pass on RC4. Then we talk about how a bot got write access to a read-only archive.

chapters.title: Chapter 2 · Write Access
chapters.synopsis: RC3's root cause is fixed, but a read-only archive does not open itself. Someone gave release-bot the keys, then deleted the account. To be continued.
